subject: Life Skills
title: Tax Credits vs Tax Deductions
description: A quick, practical guide to Tax Credits vs Tax Deductions.

hook.text: A $1,000 tax credit saves you $1,000. A $1,000 deduction might save you only $220.

buildup.text: A deduction lowers your taxable income. A credit directly reduces the tax you owe, dollar for dollar.

discovery.text: Credits are far more valuable. Education credits, child credits, and energy credits save the most.

twist.text: Some credits are refundable. Even if you owe zero tax, the government sends you the excess as a refund.

climax.text: Always claim eligible credits first. Then apply deductions to shrink whatever taxable income remains.

punchline.text: Credits cut your bill. Deductions just trim income.

quiz.question: How is a tax credit different from a tax deduction?
options: Credits lower taxable income; deductions lower tax owed
Credits reduce tax owed dollar for dollar; deductions lower income
They are the same thing with different names
